hero.title: A Work Agent for Studios and Agencies
hero.description: Give Floatboat an approved brief, source assets, and the next production goal. Your Work Agent prepares plans, specialist handoffs, review sets, and delivery packages in a persistent project workspace while leads retain creative and client authority.

burdens.title: A brief changes as it passes through the studio
burdens.description: A studio project moves from the client brief through specialist production to final review. These workflows connect assets, dependencies, and revision decisions across those stages, helping the team preserve client intent while keeping the next owner and delivery requirements clear.

items.label: Brief

items.label: Handoff

items.label: Review

faq.title: Work Agent questions for studios and agencies
faq.description: Practical answers about briefs, specialist craft, versions, client assets, and approval before delivery.

items.question: Is Floatboat a creative project-management system?
items.answer: No. Keep the system your studio uses for formal project tracking. Floatboat is a Work Agent that uses the project workspace to prepare handoffs, drafts, review sets, and deliverables.

items.question: Can multiple agents replace studio specialists?
items.answer: Agents can split research and production steps, but specialists still direct the work, judge craft, resolve trade-offs, and approve what represents the studio.

items.question: How does it keep the brief consistent across disciplines?
items.answer: Use one approved context, role-specific instructions, explicit dependencies, and versioned review sets instead of copying the brief into separate unconnected chats.

items.question: Can each client have different workflows and standards?
items.answer: Yes. Templates, rights, naming, review stages, deliverable formats, and approval roles should be configured per client or project.

items.question: How should confidential client assets be handled?
items.answer: Apply contract and studio policy, isolate client work where needed, grant minimum access, and inspect the processing behavior of every model and connector.

items.question: Will deliverables be sent to the client automatically?
items.answer: The recommended workflow produces a review and delivery pack. A responsible project or account lead approves files, recipients, access, and timing before release.

items.question: What is the best first studio workflow?
items.answer: Choose one current project with a stable brief and two specialist handoffs. Test whether shared context reduces clarification and version errors before broadening the workflow.

finalCta.title: Pass the approved brief without losing client intent
finalCta.description: Bundle source assets, revisions, and open feedback for the next specialist. The creative lead reviews the production handoff.
